concepts.why: The patient has a history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and presents with scaly erythematous plaques on the lateral leg.
The patient has a history of juvenile dermatomyositis and presents with symptoms consistent with a flare of the disease.

The patient presents with diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids, and violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest, consistent with psoriatic arthritis.
The patient presents with photodistributed poikiloderma on the chest, a characteristic feature of dermatomyositis.
The patient has a history of autoimmune skin conditions, including psoriasis and dermatomyositis.

The patient presents with diffuse ill-defined erythema and mild edema of the face and eyelids, and violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, periungual skin, and chest, consistent with an inflammatory skin condition.
The patient presents with difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs, consistent with a musculoskeletal condition.
The patient presents with muscle weakness, as evidenced by difficulty picking up her child and climbing stairs.
The patient has a history of psoriasis and dermatomyositis, and presents with symptoms consistent with a skin condition with systemic involvement.
The patient has a history of chronic inflammatory diseases, including psoriasis and dermatomyositis, and presents with symptoms consistent with a chronic inflammatory disease.

rationales.F01: Biopsy-proven psoriasis is a strong indicator for psoriasis.
rationales.F02: Juvenile dermatomyositis is a strong indicator for dermatomyositis.
rationales.F03: Remission of juvenile DM reduces the likelihood of active dermatomyositis.
rationales.F09: Scaly erythematous plaques are a characteristic feature of psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.
rationales.F11: Normal creatine kinase levels reduce the likelihood of active myopathy.
rationales.F12: Normal aldolase levels reduce the likelihood of active myopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of biopsy-proven psoriasis and current symptoms such as scaly erythematous plaques on the lateral leg, along with violaceous to erythematous patches on the joints, suggest a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, which explains both skin and joint findings.
